title: Power Pages: MCP server exposes site data to AI clients
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, site enablement, licensing layers and data boundaries are supported. Minor corrections should complete the app-registration path, move the Graph request-body instruction into its note, and remove the consent checklist step that has no corresponding control row.

claims.claim: The Power Pages MCP server exposes site data and operations through a standardized interface for AI clients.
claims.quote: MCP Server for Power Pages is a feature that exposes Power Pages data, APIs, and business logic through an MCP-compliant interface.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: AI clients can create, read, update and delete Dataverse records through the site's Web API.
claims.quote: Allow AI agents to interact with Power Pages Web APIs to create, read, update, and delete Dataverse records.

claims.claim: The public-preview capability lets makers enable CRUD without custom code.
claims.quote: In the public preview release, makers can enable Create, Read, Update, Delete (CRUD) operations via the site’s Web API layer without writing custom code.

claims.claim: Makers can provision the MCP endpoint through site settings.
claims.quote: Makers can provision the MCP server endpoint through site settings

claims.claim: The described release is public preview.
claims.quote: In the public preview release, makers can enable Create, Read, Update, Delete (CRUD) operations

claims.claim: MCP enables natural-language queries and changes to site data.
claims.quote: letting AI assistants query and manipulate Power Pages data conversationally through any MCP-compatible AI client.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Web roles and table permissions govern MCP access to site data.
claims.quote: perform secure CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations on Dataverse data while respecting web roles, table permissions, and authentication boundaries.

claims.claim: The MCP server respects authentication boundaries.
claims.quote: Maintain security controls: Keep full control through web roles, table permissions, and authentication boundaries.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Setup supports either Microsoft Entra ID or Microsoft Entra External ID.
claims.quote: This article shows you how to set up Microsoft Entra ID or Microsoft Entra External ID as an identity provider for your Power Pages site and configure it to expose the MCP scope.

claims.claim: MCP identity setup includes an exposed scope and a client app registration with delegated permissions.
claims.quote: follow the steps in the following sections to add a custom scope, create a new app registration, and assign delegated permissions.

claims.claim: A Copilot Studio agent can connect to the MCP server and be published to Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote:
This will create a new agent that we will publish later to Microsoft 365 Copilot.
Configure the Model Context Protocol tool to connect your agent to the Power Pages MCP Server.

claims.claim: Internal teams can perform portal operations from Copilot without navigating the portal.
claims.quote: Support internal workflows: Empower internal teams to perform portal operations without navigating the portal UI.

claims.claim: Web API access is limited to tables exposed through the site's Web API configuration.
claims.quote: To enable the portals Web API for your site, configure the site settings for each table that you want to expose.

claims.claim: Web API configuration limits which columns are exposed.
claims.quote: You can define the columns available to the Web API by listing them in a site setting, by using a Dataverse system view, or by combining both methods.

claims.claim: Column permissions can further restrict Web API access.
claims.quote: You can configure column permissions to further define privileges to individual columns within a table while using the portal Web API.

claims.claim: OAuth scopes participate in authenticating MCP clients.
claims.quote: This site setting defines the OAuth 2.0 scopes that the Power Pages runtime requests when authenticating an MCP client.

claims.claim: Bearer authentication settings configure token validation for the endpoint.
claims.quote: This setting specifies the protocol type—most commonly OpenIdConnect—used by the backend to validate tokens passed in the Authorization: Bearer <token> HTTP header.

claims.claim: The Copilot Studio client configuration uses a client secret and requires a redirect URI in the client app registration.
claims.quote:
Client Secret: Enter the client secret value
Copy the redirect URL from Copilot Studio and add it to your third-party app registration.

claims.claim: Incorrect site-setting names or values prevent the MCP server from functioning properly.
claims.quote: Incorrect site setting names or values prevent the MCP server from functioning properly. Double-check all entries before proceeding.

claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot license for end users who use the agent

claims.claim: Power Pages has a licensing requirement separate from the AI client's licence.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio use may consume credits, depending on the agent design.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits measure the time and effort your agent needs to retrieve information, respond to prompts, and use any actions or custom Azure Bot Service skills.

claims.quote: Web API calls made by authenticated users (internal or external) don't count towards page views, but require applicable authenticated user capacity licenses.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A separate charge or tariff for the Power Pages MCP server itself is not published.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages MCP server pricing licensing charge meter. Read MCP overview, client prerequisites, Power Pages licensing, Web API overview, licensing FAQ and pay-as-you-go meter excerpts; found product/client charges but no separate MCP server tariff.

claims.claim: The setup is for makers or administrators with access to a Power Pages environment.
claims.quote: Maker or admin access to the Power Pages environment

claims.claim: VS Code and Copilot Studio are examples of MCP-compatible clients.
claims.quote: Access to an MCP protocol-compatible client (VS Code, Microsoft Copilot Studio)

claims.claim: The documented setup grants admin consent after adding the MCP, openid and profile delegated permissions.
claims.quote:
Select the check box next to MCP and select Add permissions.
Select Delegated permissions, select the check boxes next to openid and profile
Select Grant admin consent for [your tenant]

claims.claim: In the Power Pages Management app, Site Settings > New reaches creation of an MCP site-setting record.
claims.quote:
Select Site Settings from the Portal Management menu.
For each setting, select New to create a new site setting record.

claims.claim: pac pages upload --path <site-folder> --modelVersion <1-or-2> uploads changed site configuration.
claims.quote:
pac pages upload --path [Folder-location] --modelVersion [ModelVersion]
Use modelVersion 1 or 2 to indicate if the site data to be uploaded will use the the standard (1) or enhanced data model (2).

claims.claim: Microsoft Entra admin center > Entra ID > App registrations reaches the app-registration control.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > App registrations and select New registration.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path and the rendered path to 'Entra ID > App registrations > New registration', as given at https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity-platform/quickstart-register-app#register-an-application.

claims.quote:
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/applications
The request body must contain displayName, which is a required property.
claims.fix: Set controls[1].api.call and its rendered call to 'POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/applications'. Prepend 'The request body must contain displayName.' to the existing note.

claims.quote:
Create a new application object.
Example 1: Create an application with the default settings

claims.claim: The non-production public-access policy is at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Products > Power Pages > Settings > Set site visibility to public access for non-production sites.
claims.quote:
select Manage.
Under Products, select Power Pages.
Select the Settings tab.
Select Set site visibility to public access for non-production sites.

claims.claim: The site-visibility row covers the policy for making non-production sites public, not the separate System administrator delegation setting.
claims.quote: Tenant admins can control whether makers can make a Power Pages site public when either the site or its environment is non-production.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no API for the non-production public-access policy as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages non-production site visibility governance policy API Power Platform Set-TenantSettings; Power Pages non-production visibility API policy. Read governance, site-visibility and Websites API reference; site visibility APIs are not this policy.

claims.claim: No tenant-wide switch for the Power Pages MCP server is documented on either the admin UI or automation surface.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages MCP server tenant-wide disable switch; Power Pages MCP tenant disable Power Platform API pac admin. Read MCP settings, pac admin excerpts and Websites API operations; no Power Pages tenant MCP toggle, distinct from Dataverse or Agent 365 controls.

claims.claim: MCP is opt-in through administrator or maker configuration and is not enabled until the required site setting turns it on.
claims.quote:
Create the required site settings to enable and configure MCP server functionality.
Enable MCP server | MCP/Enabled | true | This site setting enables or disables MCP server for the site.

claims.claim: MCP enablement is configured per site.
claims.quote: This site setting enables or disables MCP server for the site.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no admin-center inventory field identifying MCP-enabled Power Pages sites as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Pages MCP server admin center inventory MCP enabled sites. Read https://learn.microsoft.com/power-pages/admin/power-pages-inventory and its Site data field table; no MCP-enabled field is listed.

claims.claim: Site settings can also be changed through the Portal Management app.
claims.quote:
Using the Portal Management app, select Site settings under the Website section.
To edit an existing setting, select the Site Setting listed in the grid.

claims.claim: The tenant-level enableSystemAdminsToChangeSiteVisibility setting determines whether System administrators can change site visibility.
claims.quote: When the tenant-level setting enableSystemAdminsToChangeSiteVisibility is set to true, members of the System administrator security role can change the site visibility.

claims.claim: When enableSystemAdminsToChangeSiteVisibility is false, System administrators must belong to an exclusive Microsoft Entra security group with site-visibility permissions.
claims.quote: If the tenant-level setting enableSystemAdminsToChangeSiteVisibility is set to false, members of the System administrator security role must be a member of an exclusive security group in Microsoft Entra that has the permissions to manage site visibility.

claims.claim: The checklist instructs readers to grant admin consent without a row for that control.
claims.quote:
Grant admin consent only for the required MCP, openid and profile scopes.
The call creates the application object only; MCP scope, delegated permissions, consent and redirect URIs are configured separately.
claims.fix: Remove the At rollout checklist bullet 'Grant admin consent only for the required MCP, openid and profile scopes.' The existing app-registration row does not document the consent control.
